test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 19 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: In 2025, which two Indian cities were recognised as 'Wetland Cities'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Udaipur and Indore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC)** officially submitted nominations for **Indore (Madhya Pradesh)**, **Udaipur (Rajasthan)**, and **Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh)** for the **Wetland City Accreditation (WCA)** under the **Ramsar Convention**.
 
• **Udaipur**, popularly known as the **City of Lakes**, is famous for its sophisticated lake system, including **Lake Pichola**, **Fateh Sagar**, and **Swaroop Sagar**, which are vital for the city's microclimate and tourism. ***Hence, the inclusion of Udaipur is correct.***
 
• **Indore** has been recognized for its environmental initiatives, particularly the restoration and protection of **Sirpur Wetland** and **Yashwant Sagar**, both of which are **Ramsar Sites**. ***Hence, the inclusion of Indore is correct.***
 
• The **Wetland City Accreditation** scheme was established to recognize cities that have taken exceptional steps to safeguard their urban wetlands and promote sustainable use.
 
• These nominations represent India's first-ever attempt to get its cities recognized on the global stage as **Wetland Cities**, highlighting the country's commitment to the **Amrit Dharohar** initiative. ***Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wetland City Accreditation (WCA):**
 
 
• This voluntary accreditation system was introduced during the **COP12** of the **Ramsar Convention** in **2015**.
 
• It aims to promote the conservation and wise use of **urban and peri-urban wetlands**, as well as sustainable socio-economic benefits for local populations.
 
• To be eligible, a city must have one or more **Ramsar Sites** or significant wetlands within its jurisdiction that provide various **ecosystem services**.
 
 
 
• **The Ramsar Convention:**
 
 
• Signed in **1971** in the Iranian city of **Ramsar**, it is one of the oldest inter-governmental accords for preserving the ecological character of wetlands.
 
• India currently has **85 Ramsar Sites** (as of 2024 updates), covering a significant area of the country's total geographical surface.
 
 
 
• **Specific City Highlights:**
 
 
• **Udaipur:** The lakes here are managed by the **Rajasthan Government** and local communities, ensuring a balance between urban development and ecological preservation.
 
• **Indore:** Known as India’s cleanest city, it has integrated waste management with wetland conservation, significantly improving the biodiversity of **Sirpur Lake**.
 
• **Bhopal:** Although not paired in the chosen option, it was also nominated due to the **Bhoj Wetland**, which consists of the **Upper Lake** and **Lower Lake**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Accreditation:** Gaining **Wetland City** status provides international prestige and helps cities attract funding for conservation projects and sustainable **eco-tourism**.
 
• **Conservation Laws:** In India, wetlands are protected under the **Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017**, which prohibit activities like encroachment, dumping of solid waste, and discharge of untreated effluents.
 
• **Global Context:** There are currently very few accredited **Wetland Cities** globally (mostly in China, France, and South Korea), and India's inclusion would mark a significant milestone for **South Asia**.
 
• **Year of Recognition:** While the nomination process gained momentum in **2024**, the official recognition status for the cycle is often finalized by the **Ramsar Secretariat** in the following year, matching the **2025** timeframe mentioned in the query.
